issues.legal_issue: An exemption from rent-control protections is invalid when the government grants it without considering whether the applicant has shown a ground relevant to the purpose of the legislation.
material_facts: A public educational trust owned rental property and used the rental income for the school it maintained.
The trust sought an exemption, asserting that the rental income was devoted to the trust’s expenses.
The trust did not claim that it needed the premises for its own use or that the rent was inadequate to meet the trust’s expenses.
The government granted the exemption, but its returns did not disclose a policy-relevant ground for doing so or establish that it had applied its mind to the relevant considerations.
issues.conclusion: The exemption notification was properly quashed because the government had not applied its mind to whether a ground germane to the Act’s policy justified the exemption; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(2) of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, the government’s exemption power must be exercised consistently with the policy and purpose of the Act. The fact that an institution falls within a qualifying category and uses the property’s income for its purposes permits it to apply, but does not by itself justify an exemption; the government must consider relevant grounds for granting it. The Court relied on P. J. Irani v. State of Madras, which held that an exemption under the analogous Section 13 of the Madras Building (Lease and Rent Control) Act, 1949, could be ultra vires if its grounds were not germane to the Act’s policy, and on Sadhu Singh v. District Board, Gurdaspur.

predicates.appeal_against_quashing_of_rent_control_: The proceeding is an appeal against a decision quashing an exemption from rent-control protections.
predicates.applicant_only_showed_qualifying_institu: The applicant relied on its qualifying institutional status and use of property income for its purposes, without showing why an exemption was needed on a ground relevant to the law’s purpose.
predicates.government_record_disclosed_no_relevant_: The government’s record disclosed no relevant ground showing that it had considered why the exemption should be granted.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the quashing of a rent-control exemption, an exemption is invalid if the applicant showed only qualifying institutional status and use of income and the government’s record disclosed no relevant ground for granting it.
